case_name: Minor Anu vs Ratan Lal Sharma

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Minors Anu @ Atul and Manu @ Abhijit (sons)

facts_of_case: The father was married to Smt. Padamja, and they had two sons. Proceedings under Section 125, Cr.P.C were initiated for interim maintenance allowance. The trial court initially granted Rs. 500/- p.m., but this was set aside by the High Court. Later, the trial court awarded Rs. 250/- p.m. as interim maintenance allowance.

legal_principles.principle: An interlocutory order is not a final decision of the whole controversy.
legal_principles.held: Ordinarily and generally the expression 'interlocutory order' is understood and taken to mean as converse to the term 'final order'.
cited_cases: Halsbury's Laws of England, Third Edition

legal_principles.principle: A final judgment is one that once puts an end to the action by declaring that the plaintiff has either entitled himself, or has not, to recover the remedy he sues for.
legal_principles.held: Four different tests for ascertaining the finality of a judgment or order have been suggested :--
cited_cases: S. Kuppuswami Rao v. The King: AIR 1949 F.C. 1
Mohoan Lal Magan Lal Thakkar v. State of Rajasthan : AIR 1968 SC 733

outcome.final_order: The appeals were allowed and the order awarding interim maintenance allowance at the rate of Rs. 250/- p.m. was set aside.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: representing minor children in family court
